title: Banana-Walnut Pancakes
changes_from_base: The same buttermilk and soured cream batter, but each pancake is scattered with sliced banana and toasted walnuts before it is flipped.
summary: Soft buttermilk pancakes scattered with sliced banana and toasted walnuts for a comforting breakfast with crunch.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle
wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
ripe bananas, quartered lengthways and thinly sliced

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 93°C, spray the wire rack with oil and set it on its tray.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 283 g plain flour with 2 tbsp caster sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ½ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk 480 ml buttermilk, 2 eggs, 60 ml soured cream and 42 g melted butter in another bowl, pour this into a well in the flour mix and stir gently until just combined and lumpy, then rest the batter 10 min.

steps.title: Mix Topping
steps.text: Mix the sliced bananas with 60 g toasted chopped walnuts.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in a 30 cm non-stick pan over medium heat, wipe out leaving a thin film, then cook 4 pancakes of 60 ml batter until the edges set, the base turns golden and bubbles begin to break, 2-3 min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Sprinkle 1 tbsp of the banana and walnut mixture over each pancake, flip and cook until golden, a further 1-2 min.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Serve straight away or keep warm on the rack, repeating with the rest of the batter and adding more oil as needed.

tips: Use ripe bananas so they soften quickly into the batter as the pancakes cook.
Toast the walnuts beforehand to bring out their flavour before scattering them on.
Keep the pan lightly oiled rather than greasy so the pancakes brown evenly.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
